lxc_905fc54d0b176bac.text: In France, the law guarantees a lunch break and the 35-hour week sets a clear limit on working time.

lxc_9c4bc1140db2ca42.text: In the USA, the car brought the meal to the driver's seat, and in Japan, longer working days turned a packed box into a daily habit.

lxc_3a5695099de1ed58.text: All three are hungry, and all three solve the problem differently.

lxc_538c988fc077be88.text: But look closely, and you find rules, roads and history doing much of the work.

lxc_208e5c03a160082a.text: Many people picture the French lunch as long and slow, with wine and several courses.

lxc_22549d29dbda6e06.text: The real rules tell a more ordered story.

lxc_ddc69e3c2b0b81ac.text: In France, the legal full-time workweek is 35 hours, and work beyond that counts as overtime.

lxc_69b594b8457b65f2.text: A working day can last up to 10 hours.

lxc_eecd66e473699d55.text: In special cases, such as a very busy period or the needs of how a company is organised, it can last up to 12 hours.

lxc_67e1570dd8700f1c.text: So the 35-hour week does not simply mean short days.

lxc_ffd3e86fb737aa90.text: It sets a clear limit, and extra hours have a cost.

lxc_65ced6679a0245f8.text: After six hours of work in a row, an employee must get a break of at least 20 minutes, and lunch counts as that break.

lxc_eb583b27c55feec6.text: In practice, lunch breaks are often longer, at around 45 minutes.

lxc_9dd58616e1826ad2.text: That is real time to sit down and eat, but it is not the two-hour meal of the stereotype.

lxc_5756e7a88bd5680a.text: This is because employees are not under their employer's direction during the break.

lxc_f70703d310c8c9a9.text: The time belongs to them, not to the company.

lxc_69fa58ac2753f38a.text: The law even shapes the place where people eat.

lxc_60310c57164db38b.text: Companies with 50 or more employees must provide a room where staff can store food, heat it and sit down.

lxc_3864d2438a04cb72.text: Think about the message behind this rule.

lxc_22eaecba5a307eb2.text: Eating is treated as something that deserves a proper space, not something you do quickly at your desk.

lxc_3bb43f879a110b05.text: This fits a wider French culture that values enjoying food.

lxc_522d54f20f805778.text: Still, the picture is not frozen.

lxc_b26c57d9f8444f60.text: Fast food and American eating habits put pressure on French food culture, especially among young people.

lxc_16299a46d889b1ed.text: Many French people protect traditional food culture through education and laws.

lxc_7408704bbbc9f4bc.text: In the United States, the average adult commute took 26.8 minutes in 2014.

lxc_ea673f36a1e9a228.text: That is one way, so a return trip comes to nearly an hour every working day.

lxc_422baa422cfd7534.text: Like many countries, the US has morning and evening rush hours, when roads and transport become crowded and slow.

lxc_699801af65c97c1b.text: Car use is widespread in the United States, and it changed how people eat.

lxc_2ccd634d6144a7e6.text: It made drive-in and drive-through restaurants popular.

lxc_77c958bb63d8c96b.text: At a drive-through, you order, pay and collect your food without leaving your seat.

lxc_6d280671750c4664.text: When the car is at the center of daily movement, the meal has to come to the car.

lxc_9432bbc37fac6342.text: Food must be quick to serve and easy to eat on the move.

lxc_c79a2b74fb5583da.text: This helps explain why American eating today puts a strong focus on fast food and take-out.

lxc_1324798668d3ce47.text: Familiar examples include burgers, pizza, hot dogs, fried foods and milkshakes.

lxc_e9bf0592bd443131.text: But this is only half the story.

lxc_faedf5a99c2f481a.text: American take-out comes from many different ethnic origins.

lxc_aaaf6fcc129484f6.text: Food variety in the US grew in the 20th century because of technology, wars, science and immigration.

lxc_d96a4983f91e9f12.text: Barbecue and Tex-Mex dishes show how strongly food can belong to one region.

lxc_1504ef628955cd95.text: The large size of the country contributes to this regional variation.

lxc_937d8bd7e32319ef.text: So "American food" is less a single menu than many local menus, connected by long roads.

lxc_c3b991c38a1c8f3a.text: Japan offers a third answer to the same question: how do you eat when work keeps you away from home?

lxc_2f46cc9a76c534a4.text: The answer was to pack the meal.

lxc_a9100a02d89a6cfe.text: A bento is a single-portion packed meal, usually for lunch.

lxc_6cb154526edb570c.text: It normally contains rice or noodles, fish or meat, and pickled or cooked vegetables in a box with separate sections.

lxc_999a5ca875e3c533.text: Lunch itself was not always normal in Japan.

lxc_de6ac3ce12279d46.text: It became common only from the early 18th century, when kerosene lamps let people stay active for longer.

lxc_a82b608c2c12d4d5.text: As working days grew longer, workers started bringing bentos to work.

lxc_14deac8fcd3b672f.text: The chain of cause is clear here.

lxc_d907d65f1922bb51.text: Light changed the length of the day, and a longer day created a new meal.

lxc_5653dc202485b78c.text: They carried wooden bento boxes called menpa, filled with barley rice and pickled plums.

lxc_ebf7ebf3b52bae45.text: This food stayed fresh even when it was cold, which mattered when there was nowhere to heat it.

lxc_337d00eeba0bd3d6.text: On long days such as rice planting, villagers shared large wooden buckets of rice balls and side dishes and ate together.

lxc_9c2ba5ef58d22ea2.text: Bentos also went to the theater.

lxc_7513995219cfe575.text: Makunouchi bentos, with grilled rice balls, fish cakes and simmered dishes, were served during breaks between acts.

lxc_ed4c329f0d659066.text: The style is still common today.

lxc_7ab327e8eb0402a4.text: In the US, hot food is handed to people who travel by car.

lxc_8f79325c4766bdb7.text: In Japan, a balanced meal is packed so it still works at room temperature.

lxc_bca76c18cc804715.text: In Tokyo, commuting is commonly linked with trains rather than cars.

lxc_b5f0f51c3e924ab6.text: A meal in a box needs no kitchen, no counter and no car, so you can carry it anywhere.

lxc_2c906ae24763b003.text: Laws and transport shape when and how people eat.

lxc_57d6e7a6f50e184c.text: Geography helps shape what they eat.

lxc_aa3346c3ad489dbf.text: Japan is a country of islands with wide access to the sea, and this explains why seafood is so important in its cooking.

lxc_1f5a658075ed8004.text: A traditional Japanese meal centers on rice and miso soup.

lxc_dca8b8b9a5493114.text: Side dishes such as fish, pickled vegetables and cooked vegetables are chosen to reflect the season.

lxc_294a39326660f086.text: The United States is the opposite case: a huge continent.

lxc_1b303b08debc12e8.text: Its scale contributes to strong regional differences in food and eating habits.

lxc_ff1154346d163c08.text: Distance works in two directions here.

lxc_13493bc28d57d20e.text: It lets each region develop its own dishes, and it also makes the car, and so the drive-through, part of everyday life.

lxc_76646a934600eb17.text: France's food story is long rather than wide.

lxc_cdfa00e73a707575.text: French cooking goes back to the 14th century, with cheese and wine as major parts.

lxc_9dd5398fd6953f06.text: In the 20th century, the chef Escoffier codified modern haute cuisine, which means he set out its rules in an organised way.

lxc_c49562f06ddcb5ae.text: Yet the everyday start of the day can be very simple.

lxc_82af222b9164819b.text: A typical French breakfast is quick: bread with butter or jam, and a café au lait.

lxc_8135f1a787f4bead.text: Each of these images hides a cause.

lxc_63c379b55902fd20.text: The American meal follows the car across a huge country.

lxc_7c66076c3ce394df.text: The Japanese bento grew from longer working days and a need for food that travels well.

lxc_4c26eb60d4bf8684.text: These are also patterns, not rules.

lxc_a37edd2415b970cd.text: Young French people feel the pull of fast food, and American food changes from one region to the next.

lxc_a86a5eb65747a67c.text: Personality alone did not create these habits.

lxc_847fefcc53ba5a39.text: They grew from systems that people built and from landscapes they live in.
